container_info.description: A native application for users to create, manage, and organize notes. The app provides basic CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) functionality for note-taking.
container_info.reasoning: The Application Description calls the app a native application for creating and managing notes. 'native' is provided explicitly in the Framework field and takes precedence. A notes app described as native most commonly maps to a desktop (or platform-native) GUI application rather than a web/mobile/backend service. The container includes runtimes and toolchains (node, python, dotnet) that can support native desktop frameworks, but because the user specified 'native' it is used as the detected framework and desktop is the most appropriate platform type for a native notes application.
requirements: Core runtime for chosen native stack only (pick one):
- For Tauri: rust toolchain (rustup + cargo) and nodejs for frontend build
- For .NET MAUI: dotnet-sdk-8.0 (present) and minimal workloads if building
- For PyQt: python3 and python3-pip (present) and PyQt5/6 package
Install only essential build tools: build-essential (present) and cargo/rustup only if using Tauri
Minimal frontend tooling if using web-based UI: yarn or npm and a simple bundler (present); no heavy devservers required beyond build step
File-based storage: use local filesystem or SQLite (install python sqlite3 or use node-sqlite3) instead of PostgreSQL/MySQL
Headless build config: non-interactive build scripts (npm run build or dotnet publish) and environment variables for CI
Minimal testing: lightweight test runner only (jest for JS if frontend tests needed, or pytest for Python) with one smoke test
No production servers, monitoring, or optional plugins; avoid installing extra DB servers (postgresql/mysql/mongodb) unless explicitly required
Version control: git (present) and basic CI-friendly scripts for build and run
Entrypoint: a simple start script to run the built native binary or electron main process in headless container for automated agents (no GUI display forwarding; use headless tests or unit tests)

steps.name: environment
steps.description: Prepare workspace, validate Node/NPM versions, ensure sqlite3 system binary present, and create a single idempotent /etc/profile.d entry that exposes the workspace node bin and sets NODE_ENV only if unset. Use atomic sudo operations for reading/writing profile file and print detected versions for traceability.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/note-organizer-206538-206547/notes_native_app"
mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
# validate node/npm
if ! command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "node/npm not available" >&2; exit 2; fi
NODE_VER=$(node -v) || true; NPM_VER=$(npm -v) || true
# require Node >=16
NODE_MAJOR=$(node -v | sed -E 's/v([0-9]+).*/\1/')
if [ "$NODE_MAJOR" -lt 16 ]; then echo "Unsupported Node version: $NODE_VER (require >=16)" >&2; exit 3; fi
# ensure sqlite3 binary exists
if ! command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apt-get update -q && sudo apt-get install -y -q sqlite3 ca-certificates || { echo 'apt install sqlite3 failed' >&2; exit 4; }; fi
command -v sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "sqlite3 missing after install" >&2; exit 5; }
# create single /etc/profile.d file atomically with sudo, set PATH and conditional NODE_ENV
PROF="/etc/profile.d/notes_native_env.sh"
SVC_CONTENT="export PATH=\"/usr/local/bin:$WORKSPACE/node_modules/.bin:\$PATH\"\n[ -z \"\${NODE_ENV-}\" ] && export NODE_ENV=development\n"
TMP=$(mktemp)
printf "%s" "$SVC_CONTENT" >"$TMP"
sudo sh -c "cmp -s '$TMP' '$PROF' 2>/dev/null || cat '$TMP' > '$PROF'"
sudo chmod 0755 "$PROF" || true
rm -f "$TMP"
# print versions for traceability
echo "node=$NODE_VER npm=$NPM_VER sqlite3=$(sqlite3 --version 2>/dev/null || echo 'unknown')"

steps.name: electron system libs
steps.description: Idempotently install a minimal set of OS libraries required by Electron on Ubuntu 24.04. Verify package availability in apt cache, skip unavailable packages with a warning, and install only missing ones. Verify critical libs after install.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# minimal Electron deps for Ubuntu 24.04
PKGS=(libgtk-3-0 libnss3 libxss1 libgbm1 libasound2 lsb-release ca-certificates)
MISSING=()
for p in "${PKGS[@]}"; do dpkg -s "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || MISSING+=("$p"); done
if [ ${#MISSING[@]} -gt 0 ]; then sudo apt-get update -q || { echo 'apt-get update failed' >&2; exit 6; }; # check availability
  AVAIL=()
  for p in "${MISSING[@]}"; do apt-cache policy "$p" | grep -q 'Candidate:' && AVAIL+=("$p") || echo "package $p not available in repos, skipping" >&2; done
  if [ ${#AVAIL[@]} -gt 0 ]; then sudo apt-get install -y -q "${AVAIL[@]}" || { echo 'apt-get install failed' >&2; exit 7; }; fi
fi
# verify critical libs
for p in libgtk-3-0 libnss3 libxss1; do dpkg -s "$p" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Required package $p missing after install" >&2; exit 8; }; done

steps.name: project scaffolding
steps.description: Create idempotent project scaffold in workspace. Ensure presence of package.json, src/main.js, renderer, webpack.renderer.js, __tests__/smoke.test.js and a deterministic start.sh. If any artifact is missing create it. This prevents partially-created scaffolds from being treated as complete.

steps.name: install dependencies
steps.description: Install project-local npm dependencies reproducibly (npm ci when package-lock.json exists, otherwise npm i and generate a lockfile). Validate that local binaries (electron, webpack, jest) are present. Validate sqlite3 native binding by opening an in-memory DB and executing a trivial query. Do NOT write /etc/profile.d here (consolidated to env-01).
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/note-organizer-206538-206547/notes_native_app"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
# retry-friendly install wrapper
attempts=0; until [ $attempts -ge 3 ]; do
  if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then npm ci --no-audit --no-fund --quiet && break; else npm i --no-audit --no-fund --quiet && break; fi
  attempts=$((attempts+1)); sleep 2
done
if [ $attempts -ge 3 ]; then echo 'npm install failed after retries' >&2; exit 11; fi
# ensure local binaries exist, fail if missing to avoid npx network fetch
for b in electron webpack jest; do
  if [ ! -x "node_modules/.bin/$b" ]; then echo "required local binary node_modules/.bin/$b missing; ensure npm install succeeded" >&2; exit 12; fi
done
# stronger sqlite3 validation: open in-memory DB and run a query
node -e "(async()=>{const sqlite3=require('sqlite3').verbose(); const db=new sqlite3.Database(':memory:'); await new Promise((res,rej)=>db.run('CREATE TABLE t(x INT)',err=>err?rej(err):res())); await new Promise((res,rej)=>db.run('INSERT INTO t(x) VALUES(1)',err=>err?rej(err):res())); await new Promise((res,rej)=>db.get('SELECT x FROM t', (err,row)=>err?rej(err):res())); db.close(); console.log('sqlite3-db-ok');})().catch(e=>{console.error('sqlite3 runtime validation failed',e); process.exit(13);})"

steps.name: testing
steps.description: Run lightweight tests (jest) and perform a headless start of the local electron binary in NODE_ENV=test to verify startup artifact creation. Start electron in its own process group (setsid), ensure no leftover processes from prior runs, wait with configurable timeout/backoff, and terminate the process group cleanly with SIGTERM then SIGKILL fallback.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/note-organizer-206538-206547/notes_native_app"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
export NODE_ENV=test
# run jest via local binary
node_modules/.bin/jest --runInBand || { echo 'jest tests failed' >&2; exit 14; }
# ensure no leftover electron processes under this workspace
pkill -f "$WORKSPACE" || true
# remove artifact and start electron in its own session
rm -f "$WORKSPACE/startup.txt"
setsid "$WORKSPACE/node_modules/.bin/electron" . >/dev/null 2>&1 &
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= $! | tr -d ' ')
[ -n "$PGID" ] || PGID=$(ps -o pgid= $! | tr -d ' ')
# wait for startup.txt with configurable timeout
TIMEOUT=${TEST_TIMEOUT:-60}
SLEEP=0.5; ELAPSED=0
while [ $ELAPSED -lt $TIMEOUT ]; do
  if [ -f "$WORKSPACE/startup.txt" ]; then break; fi
  sleep "$SLEEP"
  ELAPSED=$(awk "BEGIN{print $ELAPSED+$SLEEP}")
  SLEEP=$(awk "BEGIN{print $SLEEP*1.5}")
done
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/startup.txt" ]; then echo 'startup artifact missing in test run' >&2; # cleanup
  if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 2; kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
  exit 15
fi
# stop process group gracefully
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 3; kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi

steps.name: build
steps.description: Build renderer assets with webpack (renderer-only). Prefer local node_modules/.bin/webpack; if missing, check for global webpack and print versions. Fail explicitly if no usable webpack is available to avoid npx network fetches.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/note-organizer-206538-206547/notes_native_app"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
if [ -x "node_modules/.bin/webpack" ]; then node_modules/.bin/webpack --config webpack.renderer.js --mode=production; else
  if command -v webpack >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "Using global webpack: $(webpack --version 2>/dev/null || true)"; webpack --config webpack.renderer.js --mode=production; else echo 'webpack binary missing locally and globally; run install step' >&2; exit 16; fi
fi
[ -f dist/renderer.js ] || { echo 'renderer build output missing' >&2; exit 17; }

steps.name: validation
steps.description: Validate the full environment: run the workspace start script (which invokes local electron), verify startup artifact content including PID and timestamp, confirm electron process group is running, then stop the process group cleanly. Depends on all prior steps.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/note-organizer-206538-206547/notes_native_app"
cd "$WORKSPACE"
export NODE_ENV=production
# ensure start.sh exists and local electron binary present
[ -x ./start.sh ] || { echo 'start.sh missing or not executable' >&2; exit 18; }
if [ ! -x "node_modules/.bin/electron" ]; then echo 'local electron binary missing; run install step' >&2; exit 19; fi
# cleanup any leftover processes
pkill -f "$WORKSPACE" || true
# start via start.sh under setsid, capture process group
setsid ./start.sh >/dev/null 2>&1 &
MAIN_PID=$!
PGID=$(ps -o pgid= $MAIN_PID | tr -d ' ')
# wait for artifact
TIMEOUT=${VALIDATION_TIMEOUT:-90}
SLEEP=0.5; ELAPSED=0
while [ $ELAPSED -lt $TIMEOUT ]; do
  if [ -f "$WORKSPACE/startup.txt" ]; then break; fi
  sleep "$SLEEP"
  ELAPSED=$(awk "BEGIN{print $ELAPSED+$SLEEP}")
  SLEEP=$(awk "BEGIN{print $SLEEP*1.3}")
done
if [ ! -f "$WORKSPACE/startup.txt" ]; then echo 'startup artifact missing' >&2; if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi; exit 20; fi
# validate content includes pid
grep -q "started" "$WORKSPACE/startup.txt" || { echo 'startup content invalid' >&2; if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi; exit 21; }
# ensure process group exists
if [ -n "$PGID" ] && kill -0 -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null; then :; else echo 'electron process group not running' >&2; fi
# stop gracefully
if [ -n "$PGID" ]; then kill -TERM -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; sleep 3; kill -KILL -"$PGID" 2>/dev/null || true; fi
ls -l "$WORKSPACE/startup.txt"

dependencies: electron (project devDependency installed by install step)
reasoning: Choose Electron because nodejs/npm are already present. The plan consolidates environment persistence into a single environment step, ensures idempotent scaffolding (creates missing artifacts even if package.json exists), avoids npx network fallbacks by requiring local workspace binaries (fail clearly if missing), strengthens sqlite3 validation by exercising the Database API, and hardens process lifecycle handling by running Electron in its own process group and terminating the group. Build metadata corrected and minimized steps preserved. Scripts use the authoritative workspace path and follow non-interactive, idempotent, and CI-friendly constraints. The approach prioritizes fail-fast deterministic behavior (no implicit network fetches at runtime), clear error codes and messages, and minimal OS package installs limited to essential Electron runtime libs available on Ubuntu 24.04.

change_logs.message: Refined plan to address analyst feedback: modified env-01 to avoid unsafe PATH writing and added env-02 to validate/install required Electron native libs; changed scaffold-01 to only generate package.json with pinned dependency versions and a main that includes SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers and avoids BrowserWindow in test mode; replaced deps-01 (renamed to install-01) to perform a single, reproducible npm install (npm ci when lockfile) and to fail if required modules are not resolvable; updated test-01 to run a smoke test that verifies startup artifact creation in NODE_ENV=test; updated validation-01 to build via webpack and start the app with the electron runtime binary (npx electron .), wait for artifact, and stop gracefully. These changes address critical issues: electron must be started by electron binary, native OS libs validated, no unsafe PATH persistence, pinned electron version, single responsibility for installs, and stronger failure detection. Modified steps: env-01, scaffold-01, deps-01 -> install-01, test-01, validation-01; added env-02 for native libs validation/installation.

Refined plan to address analyst feedback: modified scaffold-01 to stop bundling main (set package.json.main to src/main.js), use ELECTRON_VER variable correctly, and create an idempotent workspace start script (start.sh). Added a new build step build-01 (script_name 'build') to run webpack for renderer only. Updated env-01 to add Node/Electron compatibility check and make NODE_ENV persistence conditional and idempotent. Updated env-02 to include additional common Electron libs (libu2f-udev, libxkbcommon0) and avoid hiding apt errors. Modified install-01 to fix /etc/profile.d PATH write to reference WORKSPACE node_modules/.bin without command substitution at creation-time and to validate native sqlite3 binding loads after install. Updated test-01 and validation-01 to prefer direct invocation of $WORKSPACE/node_modules/.bin/electron, increase startup wait with backoff, and use deterministic binaries. These changes address HIGH/CRITICAL items: no bundling of main to avoid native module breakage, explicit build step, deterministic local binary invocation, Node/Electron compatibility checks, idempotent profile.d writes, native binding validation, and addition of workspace start script.

Refined plan addressing analyst feedback: consolidated /etc/profile.d writes into env-01 and removed duplicate writes from install-01; made env-01 add explicit version checks and atomic sudo read/write for profile file (modified env-01). Added defensive package availability checks and limited OS libs to minimal required set in env-02; log/skips unavailable packages (modified env-02). Made scaffold-01 idempotent for all required artifacts (package.json, start.sh, src/main.js, webpack.renderer.js, __tests__/smoke.test.js) instead of exiting early when package.json exists (modified scaffold-01). Removed npx fallbacks: install-01 now installs devDependencies and errors if local binaries (electron, webpack, jest) are missing; install-01 also replaces the shallow sqlite3 require with a small runtime validation that opens an in-memory DB and runs a query (modified install-01). test-01 and validation-01 now launch electron in a dedicated process group using setsid, ensure no leftover electron processes in workspace before starting, wait with configurable timeout/backoff, and terminate the whole process group with SIGTERM then SIGKILL fallback; PID handling and timeouts improved (modified test-01, validation-01). Corrected build-01 category to 'build' and removed npx --no-install fallback, preferring local webpack or global with version print and explicit failure if missing (modified build-01). Overall changes address CRITICAL and HIGH recommendations: single /etc/profile.d writer, idempotent scaffolding, no npx network fallbacks, robust sqlite3 validation, reliable process lifecycle handling, and metadata consistency.
